title: Air-dry clay wax seal stamp holder
subtitle: A slab-built rectangular holder with indented wells for storing wax seal stamps
excerpt: A wax seal stamp holder is a slab-built rectangular tray with individual indented wells, one for each stamp handle. This version is air-dry clay with no kiln. The finished holder is 15 cm x 8 cm and holds five to six standard wax seal stamp handles upright in their wells.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. V&A open-access collection for desk accessory ceramic form reference.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat sheet of clay rolled to an even thickness, used as the building block in slab construction
The stage at which clay holds its shape firmly but remains damp enough to join, carve, and trim
The joining method: roughen both surfaces with a needle tool, apply clay slip, then press together firmly
Fully air-dried and unfired; pale, lightweight, and fragile, ready for sealing

content.text: A wax seal stamp holder is a low slab-built tray with cylindrical wells pressed into the base, each sized to hold the handle of a wax seal stamp upright. Air-dry clay needs no kiln. The finished tray is 15 cm x 8 cm x 2 cm and holds five to six stamps with their decorative heads facing up for immediate selection.

materials.name: Clay slip (same clay body, thinned to double-cream consistency with water)

content.text: Preparation

Measure your wax seal stamp handles before making the wells. Most standard handles are 10-12 mm in diameter at the shaft. The wells are formed by pressing a cylinder into the soft clay base: a thick pencil or a short section of wooden dowel in the right diameter works well. If your handles vary in size, make the wells slightly oversize so any handle fits. Work on a canvas sheet. Roll the
slab
with guide rods on each side for an even 6 mm thickness.
Making the base
Roll a slab 6 mm thick. Cut a rectangle 17 cm x 10 cm for the base floor. This is slightly larger than the finished tray size to allow for the wall thickness on each side.

While the base is still soft, press your stamp handle (or a pencil or dowel of matching diameter) into the clay at regular intervals to form the wells. Press each cylinder 10 mm deep into the base. Space the wells evenly: if making five wells, space them approximately 2.5 cm apart along the length of the tray. Twist the cylinder slightly as you remove it to avoid pulling the clay up with the form.

Check each well is clean inside: run the needle tool around the interior of each well to smooth any rough edges. The well depth should not punch through the base: stop at 10 mm, which leaves at least 6 mm of clay below.
Allow the base to stiffen for 30-40 minutes until it is firm enough to lift without distorting the wells.
Adding the walls
Roll a second slab 6 mm thick. Cut four wall strips: two at 17 cm x 2.5 cm (long sides) and two at 10 cm x 2.5 cm (short sides). These will form the low walls around the tray perimeter.
Use the needle tool to
score and slip
the bottom edges of each wall strip and the corresponding perimeter of the base. Press each wall strip upright in turn, blending the interior join with a wooden rib.
At the corners, score and slip the abutting ends of the wall strips before pressing them together. Blend all interior corners with a damp wooden rib.
Smooth the top rim of all four walls with a damp pottery sponge. Level the rim by pressing gently with a flat tool if any sections are uneven.
Surface decoration (optional)
At the
leather-hard
stage, press a pottery stamp or a lace piece against the exterior long walls for texture. Work on one wall at a time, supporting the interior with your other hand to prevent the wall from bowing.
Use the needle tool to carve initials or a small motif into the exterior short wall. The 2.5 cm height gives enough space for one or two small letters.
Drying

Allow the tray to dry slowly at room temperature. Air-dry clay shrinks as it dries: the tray floor may pull inward slightly at the corners. This is normal. If the floor begins to warp upward at the edges, place a light flat weight (a small smooth book) across the base while it is still at leather-hard to hold it flat. The tray reaches
bone-dry
in two to three days when it is pale throughout and no longer cool to the touch. Do not rush drying with a hairdryer or oven: forced drying causes corner cracking.
Finishing

Apply two coats of 50/50 PVA and water to all surfaces including the well interiors. The PVA coat hardens the surface and makes the clay wipe-clean. If painting with acrylics, do so after the first PVA coat is dry but before the second coat: the painted surface is then locked under the final PVA layer.
Care

The tray is a decorative desk organiser. Wipe with a dry cloth. Do not submerge in water. Wax drips from stamps will not damage the clay surface but can be peeled off once set. Keep away from direct sunlight, which fades acrylic paint over time.
Variations
Add a small well at one short end sized to hold a wax stick upright, approximately 12 mm in diameter. This keeps the wax stick accessible alongside the stamps.
Make a matching ink pad tray: a shallower version with no wells, just a flat 10 cm x 10 cm base with 15 mm walls, large enough for one ink pad to rest inside.

Personalise the short-end walls with pressed letter stamps in the clay while still soft, spelling out a name or word. Press the letters one at a time at a 90-degree angle, rocking the stamp side to side to ensure even impression.

items.problem: Wells cracked around the rim during drying
items.cause: The clay around the well rim was too thin after pressing; the form removed too much clay depth
items.fix: At leather-hard, fill small cracks with a paste of clay and water and smooth over. For future pieces, stop pressing wells at 8 mm depth to leave more clay thickness around the rim

items.problem: Base warped upward at the corners during drying
items.cause: Uneven drying; the base edges dried faster than the centre
items.fix: At leather-hard, place a smooth flat weight on the base and leave for 24 hours. If already bone-dry and warped, it cannot be corrected: glue a small felt pad to the raised corner as a foot to level it

items.problem: Wall corners split at the joins
items.cause: Insufficient scoring or slip at the corner joins, or the clay was too dry at joining time
items.fix: Dampen the crack, score both faces, apply fresh slip, and press together. Support from outside with a thin clay coil while drying

items.problem: Stamp handle does not fit in the well after drying
items.cause: Clay shrank slightly on drying, reducing the well diameter
items.fix: Enlarge the well carefully with a needle tool or a piece of rolled sandpaper. Air-dry clay can be worked after drying, but go slowly to avoid cracking
